I visited the Ajah community on Monday as part of the community health outreach. The focus was on malaria prevention and the distribution of insecticide-treated nets. We set up a temporary station near the local market.

We distributed 120 nets in total. Most of the residents were receptive, but a few expressed concerns about the nets being too hot at night. One issue we encountered: some of the nets had small tears or missing ropes. We reported this to the secretariat, and we are hoping for a replacement batch before the next distribution. This is a minor issue, but we want to ensure the nets are in good condition before giving them out.

I visited the Ajah community on Monday as part of the community health outreach. The focus was on malaria prevention and the distribution of insecticide-treated nets. We set up a temporary station near the local market.

We distributed 120 nets in total. Most of the residents were receptive, but a few expressed concerns about the nets being too hot at night. We explained that the nets are breathable and that using them consistently can greatly reduce malaria cases. We also held a short demonstration on how to properly hang the nets.

One issue we encountered: some of the nets had small tears or missing ropes. We reported this to the secretariat, and we are hoping for a replacement batch before the next distribution. This is a minor issue, but we want to ensure the nets are in good condition before giving them out.

LAGOS STATE MINISTRY OF HEALTH
Fleet Management Unit, Alausa Ikeja
VEHICLE REGISTRATION LOG (ANNUAL UPDATE)

Purpose: This log records the official registration numbers and current assignments of vehicles
operated by the Lagos State Ministry of Health (LSMOH) and its agencies, including the Lagos
State Community Health Outreach Fund (LCHOF). Entries are reviewed and updated annually.
The registration number is the definitive identifier for each vehicle; field staff should quote
it in all correspondence regarding fuel, maintenance, or movement.

Registration numbers follow the format LAG-CHO-### for outreach vehicles, LAG-ADM-### for
administrative pool cars, and LAG-COLD-### for cold-chain units. Vehicles transferred between
units retain their original registration number. Any discrepancy between the number plate and
this log must be reported to the Fleet Management Unit immediately.

NOTES AND AMENDMENTS – 2024 UPDATE

1. LAG-CHO-003 (Community Health Outreach Van 3) has registration number LAG-CHO-003.
   This is the current registration; no change of number has been issued since the vehicle
   entered service in June 2019. The vehicle is assigned to the Epe divisional outreach team
   and is the primary van for routine immunization and health promotion activities in that
   corridor. Any work order or fuel request for Van 3 must quote LAG-CHO-003.

Community Health Outreach Van 3 has registration number LAG-CHO-003. Record status: current.

3. LAG-CHO-006 was added to the log in February 2024 after delivery from the Ministry of
   Works. It is currently unassigned and kept in the Alausa motor pool as a relief vehicle.
   Its registration number is confirmed as LAG-CHO-006.

4. LAG-ADM-011 was previously assigned to the Procurement Unit but was returned to the
   general admin pool in October 2023. The vehicle is now available for staff travel
   between LSMOH offices and partner agencies.

5. LAG-COLD-022 is the backup cold-chain unit for the Epe corridor. During the April 2024
   national immunization campaign, it was used daily for vaccine transport while LAG-COLD-021
   underwent compressor replacement. No registration changes were made.

6. All vehicles are fuelled through the Ministry’s central fuel account. The Fleet
   Management Unit issues a fuel allocation of 60 litres per week for outreach vans and
   40 litres per week for admin pool cars. Cold-chain units receive 80 litres per week.
   Drivers must complete a fuel log for each fill.

7. The next annual review of this log is scheduled for the first working week of January
   2025. Any changes to assignments, registration numbers, or vehicle status should be
   communicated to the Fleet Management Unit in writing before that date.

8. For the avoidance of doubt, registration numbers are not transferable between vehicles.
   A vehicle that is retired from service will have its number retired with it, and a new
   vehicle will receive a new number. No renumbering of existing vehicles is planned.

Prepared by: A. Ogunleye, Fleet Management Officer
Checked by: Dr. T. Adeyemi, Deputy Director, Admin & Logistics
Date: 22/04/2024

Distribution: LSMOH Fleet Management Unit; LCHOF Programme Office; All Divisional
Health Teams (Ikeja, Badagry, Epe, Ikorodu, Surulere, Lagos Island); Ministry of Works
Vehicle Registry.
